label: paragraph_title
text: VUCHOW- INCIDENT.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, replying to the Rt. Hon. C. P. Trevelyan (Labour, "Newcastle-on-Tyne"). in regard to the British Senior Naval Officer at Wuchow closing the port to Chinese shipping on June 24, the Rt. Hon. Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, after reciting the facts of the case, said that "His Majesty's Government still awaited detailed information, but in view of the instructions "issued by the Canton Government that facilities should be provided, it was inclined to consider that the responsibility for the incident lay with the local Chinese authorities.

label: text
text: Mr. Trevelyan asked if there was any precedent for "Naval Officers using their discretion" in relations with foreign Powers without reference for the Home Government? Sir Austen Chamberlain replied that there was plenty of precedent. Happily for the British Empire and the peace of the world our Naval Officers had shown themselves most capable of using their discretion. Ministerial cheers.

text: In the House of Commons the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs was asked whether he was aware that the British Senior Naval Officer at Wuehow had closed that port to Chinese shipping for ten hours on June 24. Sir Austen Chamberlain said that after the murder of a British subject, Mr. Phillips of the A.P.C. Charge of the British ships will be proceeding at the request of the British Acting Consultant to the neighborhood to investigate the circumstances of the serine The Canton Government said that it had ordered the local authorities to afford them all facilities at Wuehow. However, the anti-foreign organisation which the local authorities appeared at first to have been unwilling or unable to control, caused an obstruction regarding the engagement of pilots. After several days' fruitless negotiations the Senior Naval Officer was obliged to resort to other measures, and took steps to close the port it proved unnecessary, however, to stop any shipping as pilots were furnished and His Majesty's ships proceeded, British Wireless Service.

label: doc_title
text: SALT REVENUE.

label: text
text: AGREEMENT WITH CHIHI

label: text
text: The Finance Ministry and the Chihli Tupan have now formally concluded the salt agreement, providing the Chihli authorities do not interfere with the salt revenue but render assistance to the salt administration in carrying out its orders.

label: text
text: The Chihli authorities undertake to abolish and not to introduce in any form illegal taxation, and to assist the transportation of salt.

label: text
text: The Salt Administration under, takes to pay the Chihli Tupan $150,000 in the middle and end of each month, provided the administration first make provision for all loan payments, for which it is responsible under the Reorganisation Loan Agreement, and provided these sums are available for collections in the Changtu district.

label: text
text: The administration also agrees to pay certain outstanding subsidies, amounting to $450,000. Reuter.

label: text
text: SITUATION SERIOUS IN CALCUTTA.

label: text
text: Calcutta, July 20.

label: text
text: Hindus, and Mohammedans have started guejilla warfare. There have been many stabbings and assaults.

label: text
text: Five have been killed and 17 seriously hurt.

label: text
text: This morning shops were closed, and the situation is extremely serious.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The disorders this morning spread and rioting broke out. The Police were obliged to fire at a number of places and eventually controlled the situation.

text:

label: paragraph_title
text: . MIXED COURT.

label: text
text: Mr. V. K. Ting, interviewed by the "Sun Pao" confirmed the reports recently published that the negotiations regarding the "rendition of the Mixed Court had considerably progressed.

label: text
text:
He declared, "generally speaking, that the terms of the proposed agreement were the same as published in the Press," though, after consultation, the Consular Body had some alterations made.
Mr. Ting stated that the draft of the agreement had been duly approved by Marshall Sun Chuan-fang and other provincial authorities, but at least a week must elapse before it can be signed.
It will be signed in the name of the Provincial Government, though Sun Chuan-fang has reported the matter to the Waichiaopu and has asked its consent.

label: text
text: “We decided to sign, whether consent was obtained or not.”

label: text
text: After "signing the" provincial agreement, the particulars will be worked out, the most important of which are the questions in which criminal cases affect the peace and order of the Settlement, and what departments of the Court shall remain, and which shall be abolished.

label: text
text: These and other questions will be taken up by the Committee of Legal Experts comprising three Chinese and three foreigners. At present the agreement may be cancelled at any time, if the Central Government can make definite plans for the complete rendition.

label: text
text: The enforceable “period” for a provisional agreement will be three years. Mr. Ting declared that the foreign lawyers’ agitation against the Settlement was merely the result of a quicker and easier Settlement problem.

label: text
text: The foreign lawyers' delegation is going to Peking this morning to interview the Diplomatic Corps.

label: text
text: The five lawyers in the delegation are Messrs. Otto Fischer, B.D. Rodger, A.M. Preston, Du Pac Du Marsoulies and Marakami.

label: doc_title
text: TWO SHIPS ASHORE.

label: text
text: Business was practically stagnant in the City this morning. Numbers had been prevented from getting to office by the cessation of all harbour traffic and few Peak residents faced the walk down with the high wind and possibility of the typhoon striking. Peak residents who braved the journey had to surmount fallen branches of trees and other debris brought down by the gale. A visit paid to the P.W.D. and Supreme Court this morning found the former practically deserted and the latter completely so. The same applied to nearly all offices.

label: text
text: A danger with which pedes-trians were faced was that of possible falls from roofs and of sign boards. Several of these latter were noticed with broken supports and constituting a grave danger to passers by.

label: text
text: "Water-gates were up in all parts of Chinatown, to prevent another wash-out." The big department stores were closed and the Sun Co. had their shutters nailed down.

label: text
text: Spectators were on the waterfront. Motor vehicles found no great difficulty in proceeding and there were ricshas aplenty.

label: text
text: Enguities made by the "China Mail" this warning elicited the information that it was not thought that the present unfavourable weather conditions would prevent temporary Peak train service from being brought into operation, of Saturday. The service would be between Kennedy Road and Plantation Road with the stations there as a terminal. It would perhaps be three weeks before it would be possible to resume the full service the "China Mail" representative was informed.

label: text
text: DOCTOR'S THEORY OF EFFECT ON MODERATE DRINKERS.

label: text
text: That moderate drinkers sometimes developed delirium tremens after a fall was the theory advanced by a doctor at the inquest at Chichester on William Corser, manager of the Salisbury Hotel, Lewisham.

label: text
text: He died at Chichester Hospital from delirium trémens and cardiac failure, following a fall on a concrete verandah at Bognor, where he was staying the weekend with friends.

label: text
text: He was alleged to be a moderate drinker.

label: text
text: BRIDE REFUSES TO BE MARRIED AT REGISTER OFFICE.

label: text
text: Because she "didn't like the witnesses" a bride walked out of the Register Office at Devonport, leaving the bridegroom dumb with amazement.

label: text
text: In conversation afterwards she said, "I didn't know who the witnesses were going to be till I saw them, so I refused to go on and we were married elsewhere." The Registrar said the girl de-

label: text
text: The Registrar said the girl described the ceremony as "bally rot."

label: text
text: The Mental Hospitals Committee of the L.C.C., in their report to the Council, state: "We have more than once considered whether sterilisation by surgical operation might be resorted to as a prophylactic against mental deficiency, but we have concluded that there are too many practical difficulties to enable the Council to endorse any proposal to make such a measure possible."
